pr_title: [Merged by Bors] - Always update clusters and remove per-frame allocations
pr_body:
* Refactor assign_lights_to_clusters to always clear + update clusters, even if the screen size isn't available yet / is zero. This fixes #4167. We still avoid the "expensive" per-light work when the screen size isn't available yet. I also consolidated some logic to eliminate some redundancies.
* Removed _a ton_ of (potentially very large) per-frame reallocations
  * Removed `Res<VisiblePointLights>` (a vec) in favor of  `Res<GlobalVisiblePointLights>` (a hashmap). We were allocating a new hashmap every frame, the collecting it into a vec every frame, then in another system _re-generating the hashmap_. It is always used like a hashmap, might as well embrace that. We now reuse the same hashmap every frame and dont use any intermediate collections.
  * We were re-allocating Clusters aabb and light vectors every frame by re-constructing Clusters every frame. We now re-use the existing collections.
  * Reuse per-camera VisiblePointLight vecs when possible instead of allocating them every frame. We now only insert VisiblePointLights if the component doesn't exist yet.
pr_comments: I'm curious about the perf impact; do we have a good benchmark for this?

> is it possible to get examples to run as part of CI?

Part of them already run using swiftshader.

> I'm curious about the perf impact; do we have a good benchmark for this?

I benchmarked `lighting.rs` prior to submitting this pr and the difference was in the noise. But that makes sense because there aren't that many lights in the scene (and therefore we have a smaller number of allocations + copies). We'd want to test on a scene with a large number of lights.
I think this is good to go now. Feel free to leave more feedback, but I'll merge this in the next few days if i dont hear back from anyone.

issue_context.title: multiple_windows example is broken
issue_context.body:
It panics with:
```
thread 'main' panicked at 'index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0', crates/bevy_pbr/src/render/light.rs:996:43
```

This is a regression introduced recently by #3968
@robtfm @superdump
comments: I'm thinking this is because the window doesn't exist yet for the first frame that the secondary camera is spawned, which results in a "default" screen size of `(0, 0)` in the cluster assignment algorithm / cluster assignments being skipped. Seems like a "corner case" that we missed in #3968. I'm guessing this would also be a problem for single window scenarios that behave the same way.
Skipping cluster prep when there are no clusters to assign to resolves the problem.

Did you see:
* https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/4148

and does that fix it?
I would not expect it to, as that only touches `update()` and the "core" issue is that update() isn't called because we "skip" it.

review_comments: I’d like to keep this comment as long as we have both cluster_dimensions and clusters.axis_slices. I wanted one source of truth. Alternatively make it so there is one source of truth and remove cluster_dimensions if possible.

I think adding extra code (and comments) that actively encourage the user to think about two sources of truth is worse. From my perspective, `cluster_dimensions` should be `requested_cluster_dimensions` and the `axis_slices` is the "actual cluster dimensions". If thats an accurate description, maybe a rename would suffice?

Also, should we unify terminology? If `cluster_dimensions` and `axis_slices` are referring to the exact same concept, we should pick one term. However from names alone, they aren't the same from my perspective. A `cluster_dimension.x == 1` makes it sound like it has "one dimension in the x axis", which I interpret to mean "one section". `axis_slices.x == 1` I would interpret to be "one slice" or "two sections". Those are incompatible definitions.

They are meant to be the same as far as my fuzzy brain can claim. And I prefer `cluster_dimensions` as the term. And I like the suggestion of `requested_cluster_dimensions` as a way of clarifying. This is a process of evolution as until recently some of the code further down was using `cluster_dimensions` where it should have been using `axis_slices` and I guess I hadn't been thoughtful enough about how to improve it but wanted to at least prevent confusion and misuse later.
yup! (this is the same approach used on `main`)

I think `dimensions_for_screen_size` just below would produce somewhat odd results, albeit non-zero dimensions. I guess it's ok, but it feels like it could be better like falling back to a known-sensible configuration in nonsensical situations?
I just made it gracefully handle zero screen sizes as outlined here: https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/4169#discussion_r824256927
